setup: CREATE TABLE items AS SELECT i::BIGINT AS item_id, ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'][1 + i] AS kind FROM range(4) t(i)
CREATE TABLE buys AS SELECT i::BIGINT AS buy_id, (i % 8)::BIGINT AS user_id, ((i * 3) % 4)::BIGINT AS item_id, TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' + to_days((i * 5)::INTEGER) AS ts FROM range(120) t(i)
input.pql: PREDICT LIST_DISTINCT(buys.item_id, 0, 30, days) RANK TOP 2 FOR EACH users.user_id

view.name: view_metric_ranking
view.yaml:
version: 0.1
source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.buys"
joins:
  - name: users
    source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.users"
    on: source.user_id = users.user_id
  - name: items
    source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.items"
    on: source.item_id = items.item_id
dimensions:
  - name: buy_id
    expr: source.buy_id
  - name: user_id
    expr: source.user_id
  - name: item_id
    expr: source.item_id
  - name: ts
    expr: source.ts
  - name: kind
    expr: items.kind
  - name: country
    expr: users.country
measures:
  - name: purchases
    expr: COUNT(1)

why: A ranking over named candidates through a metric view whose fact table joins two tables, users and items. The view is created in the test schema from the yaml, its sources named with the {catalog} and {schema} placeholders the capture writes (no private name), each part backtick-quoted since Databricks reads a catalog's hyphen only quoted; its joins' on keys are bare, as people write them, so PyYAML reads each as the key true (KO3-40), which the reference reads too (DB/metric_view.py:825-909, join_cfg.get(True))
